items: Curriculum
Built around NCERT and a structured concept-based syllabus; it is widely aligned with Indian competitive exams such as JEE NEET, NEET CUET.
A broader, content-rich syllabus with strong language depth and separate treatment of subjects such as History/Civics Geography from middle school onward.
-based, concept-led, and interdisciplinary with programmes such as MYP and DP designed around global-minded learning.
Assessment
More exam-led, with longer papers and many question types covering recall, understanding, application, and evaluation.
Exam-heavy but typically more descriptive and detailed with required external and internal.
Uses a mix of internal and external assessment; MYP external assessment is optional and DP adds essays, projects, and other coursework-heavy elements.
Subject flexibility
Generally more structured with fewer combinations than international curricula.
Moderate flexibility but still more fixed than IB.
Greater flexibility, especially in subject choice and in how learners connect disciplines.
Transferability
Transfers most cleanly between schools within India; CBSE also also has broadest domestic footprint.
Transfers best within CISCE schools but the smaller school network can make moves less convenient than CBSE.
Best when moving between international schools; recognition is global, but local can depend on school level and mapping.
